name: BEW World Heavyweight Title
epitaph: No dated title-history ledger survives for this belt. The fed's own served card billed the Jamie Williams vs. Devastator match as "the BEW World Title Match" and its own broadcast calls it "the header to the main event" — a distinct, earlier match than the Flesh vs. Kevin Merrix bout that actually closes the show untitled. Devastator, its billed reigning champion entering Night of Armageddon (20 March 1999), never appears in person, cutting his own promo by remote screen before losing the belt to Jamie Williams's Northern Lights Elbow — the belt's own only documented title change in the held record.

name: BEW Hardcore Title
epitaph: The fed's own broadcast bills Flesh, entering the Night of Armageddon main event, as "a seven time Hardcore champion" and "its current HARDCORE CHAMPION" — but the belt is never defended on this card; the untitled main event that follows carries no title stakes in either the broadcast's own introduction or the fed's own card page. No reign start survives, and no title change is documented in the held record.
notes: SOURCES DISAGREE with the fed's own card page, which labels the night's Extreme Warrior vs. Jonathan Prophet crucifixion match "BEW Hardcore Title Match" — the broadcast's own repeated, internally consistent dialogue instead calls that same bout a Television Title defense (see bew-television). Flesh's own concurrent Hardcore billing, entering a later match on the same show, is inconsistent with Prophet also holding that same belt that night; both documents are receipted, neither silently resolved.

name: BEW Television Title
epitaph: Defended in a no-time-limit Crucifixion match at Night of Armageddon (20 March 1999): Jonathan Prophet, its billed reigning champion, lost the belt to Extreme Warrior after both men fell through live land mines from the top turnbuckle and Prophet was nailed to a wooden cross mid-match — the belt's own only documented title change in the held record.
notes: SOURCES DISAGREE with the fed's own card page, which labels this same bout "BEW Hardcore Title Match" (see bew-hardcore) — the broadcast's own dialogue names the Television Title three separate times (Hughy's own introduction, Prophet's own billing as "its current Television champion," and the winner's call, "new Television Champion"), the stronger and more internally consistent account, preferred here; the card's own conflicting label is receipted at bew-hardcore rather than silently dropped.

name: BEW United States Title
epitaph: Defended at Night of Armageddon (20 March 1999): Flyin' Bryan Mercy, its billed reigning champion, lost the belt to James Pope's debuting Limo Wreck finisher — the belt's own only documented title change in the held record, and, per the fed's own broadcast commentary, Pope's first match in the BEW.

name: BEW Atlantic Title
epitaph: Named once, in passing: Night of Armageddon's own broadcast introduces Jaigo as "its former Atlantic Champion." No reign dates, no defense, and no successor survive in the held record — the belt is not defended anywhere on this card.
